week4_picks_results.lock: Legion -3.0 over Sleeping Giants: LOST (Giants won 147.3-143.72)
week4_picks_results.upset_watch: Boonist Monks +1.5 over Kittler: LOST (Kittler won 145.46-133.42)

rankings.blurb: Jonathan Taylor dropped 30.1 — his second time above 30 this season — and Baker Mayfield added 26.66 in a 145.46-point performance that dispatched the Boonist Monks by 12.04 and vaulted you to the top of the standings. You're 5-0 all-time against the Monks, a perfect record that's becoming less of a fun fact and more of a psychological weapon. Puka Nacua's 19.5 continued his weekly statement stretch, and Nik Bonitto chipped in 18.0 from the IDP slot. The preseason called your ceiling "drywall." Through five weeks, you're the points leader at 770.2 and the only 4-1 team that also held the number one spot in Week 1. Runner-up in 2022, runner-up in 2023, champion in 2024, and now the top seed at the quarter pole. Consistency isn't just a personality trait anymore — it's a dynasty. The defending champion reclaimed the throne, and this time it brought receipts.

The streak is over. Four games. That's how long the Cinderella slipper fit before the Sleeping Giants ripped it off your foot. Mahomes dropped 27.72, McCaffrey went for 23.9, Waddle contributed 20.0, and it wasn't enough — your 143.72 fell short of the Giants' 147.3 by 3.58 in a loss that felt like running into a wall you didn't know was there. Your Elo dipped 13.3 points but still sits at 1604.3, because one loss doesn't erase four weeks of dominance. The preseason said "since winning the inaugural title in 2022, you've been stuck in the middle." Then you went 4-0 and proved everybody wrong. Now you're 4-1 and proving that even the hottest teams have to cool down eventually. ARSB added 14.0 and DeVonta Smith kicked in 15.4, but the Giants' Kyren Williams was the wrecking ball nobody saw coming. The Voltron receivers assembled, and they still lost to a guy running through walls. The question now isn't whether you're real. It's whether one loss becomes a trend.

Three straight. The aging roster that was supposed to be selling veterans and embracing the rebuild just ended the league's only undefeated streak. Kyren Williams bulldozed for 27.1, Jalen Hurts orchestrated with 19.5, and Stefon Diggs — a name nobody had circled in preseason lineups — torched the Legion for 19.6. Your 147.3 was the highest score among 4-1 teams this week, and the win pushed your streak to three games, the longest active run in the Jailyard. The preseason ranked you eleventh. You're third now. The preseason said "if the veterans hold up you could sneak into the playoffs." You're not sneaking — you're kicking the door down with Derrick Henry's leg. Your all-time record is 39-17, the best winning percentage in league history, and the franchise that reached the 2024 championship game looks like it's plotting a return trip. The Island of Misfit WR1s has a new resident in Diggs, and suddenly the nickname feels more complimentary than cutting.

Quiet week, quiet win. Josh Allen's 20.42 wasn't his most spectacular outing, but against a Father Time team that mustered 119.42, spectacular wasn't necessary. Courtland Sutton's 13.9, Achane's 13.6, and Michael Pittman's 12.4 gave you a balanced-but-unremarkable 127.62 that was still enough to win by 8.2 and push your record to 4-1. The all-time series against Father Time is now tied at two apiece. The preseason called you "a weekly thrill ride." This week was more of a commuter train — reliable, on time, nobody talked about it. Your Elo sits at 1626.0, second-highest in the league behind only Ken-obi, and the two-game winning streak suggests the 1.64-point upset over Ken-obi in Week 4 wasn't a fluke but a turning point. Fifth in 2023, fifth in 2024, and now comfortably in the top four. The WR room is still "a meme waiting to happen," but when Josh Allen is your floor, the meme doesn't matter. Yet.

Bounce-back complete. After the 1.64-point heartbreaker to Rasheeing last week, you handled Noble FFT 140.22 to 125.26 with the quiet efficiency of a franchise that's been here before. Rachaad White led with 21.1, Sam LaPorta added 17.7, and Saquon Barkley kicked in 16.3. The 5-1 all-time record against Noble is approaching bully territory, and your Elo is at its all-time peak of 1700.2, the highest rating in the entire Jailyard. Nico Collins' 14.0 kept the WR production ticking, and even your kicker — Chase McLaughlin's 13.5 — outscored several opponents' starters. The preseason said you were "the franchise everyone measures themselves against." The Elo agrees. The loss to Rasheeing feels like a distant memory now, and the group chat's panic about whether it was "a blip or a fault line" has its answer: blip. At 4-1 with the league's highest Elo, the taxi squad debates and waiver-day alarms can resume their regularly scheduled programming.

Zero for five. You have never beaten Kittler on the Roof. Not once. Not in any season, any format, any timeline. Jaxon Smith-Njigba's 23.2 and Jake Ferguson's 20.4 gave you a respectable 133.42, but when Jonathan Taylor is dropping 30.1 on the other side, "respectable" earns you a loss and a three-spot tumble in the rankings. David Montgomery added 17.72 and Kyler Murray posted 15.3 — solid contributions from a roster that's third in total points at 762.5 but somehow 3-2. The preseason called you the instigator of side bets and polls. Bet against Kittler next time. Your Elo dropped 11.6 points, and the age cliff we keep mentioning is still lurking — Lamar, Tyreek, and Kelce can't buy you a win against a franchise that owns you. Last week you were third. This week you're sixth. The fall from the top three is the kind of correction that makes the group chat go quiet, which for you — the chat's resident instigator — is the cruelest punishment of all.

There it is. The nuclear option. Rico Dowdle — who? — erupted for 31.9, Ja'Marr Chase reminded the league why he's a top-three dynasty asset with 29.0, and your 177.94 was the highest score by any team this week by over 30 points. You beat Burden by 31.56 in the week's biggest blowout, and the WR trio we spent two weeks eulogizing just had its resurrection moment. Jayden Daniels' 17.14 gave you actual quarterback production, and Michael Carter — another name from the "who is that?" file — added 15.8. Last week we called your roster "a crime scene." This week it's the scene of a celebration. The preseason said you were a contender. Then you went 1-3 and the preseason looked like fiction. At 2-3 with 177.94 still ringing in the group chat, the contender label isn't dead — it was just on a bye. Your Elo climbed 12.5 points, and the running back problem that was supposed to sink you just got answered by a guy named Dowdle.

Last week you hung 176.42 on the defending champion. This week you lost to a 0-4 team by 2.02. That's the Jailyard in two data points. Justin Fields filled in at QB with 25.92 and Deebo Samuel contributed 19.6, but Omarion Hampton — your breakout star from last week's 25.0 eruption — came crashing back to earth with just 10.0. The all-time series against Chudders is now deadlocked at four apiece, and your Elo took an 18.4-point hit, the biggest drop of any team this week. Two weeks ago you were the breakout story. One week ago you were the team that destroyed the defending champion. Now you're 2-3 and sliding. The preseason said "pundits in the chat love to remind you that picks don't score points." Neither, apparently, do 176-point weeks when they're followed by 137-point whimpers. Hampton hitting was the condition we flagged for contention. Hampton regressing to 10.0 is the condition nobody planned for.

When your defense outscores every skill position player on your roster, something has gone fundamentally wrong. The New Orleans Saints defense dropped 25.0 — your second-highest scorer behind Javonte Williams' 26.4 — in a 125.26-point effort that Ken-obi handled by 14.96. Breece Hall managed 15.5, Tyler Warren added 12.4, and Bijan Robinson — the anchor of the league's "scariest backfield" — was conspicuously absent from the top-five scoring list. You're 1-5 all-time against Ken-obi, a series that's becoming less of a rivalry and more of a scheduled donation. The preseason ranked you second. You're ninth. Where is Caleb Williams? Where is A.J. Brown? The roster that was supposed to dominate with elite RB production is relying on a defense and Javonte Williams to carry the load. The real-life GM drafting style needs a real-life course correction, and the next five weeks will determine whether this is a stumble or a collapse.

Pop the sparkling cider — you won a game. Emeka Egbuka erupted for 27.8, Jacory Croskey-Merritt added 26.0 from the waiver-wire wilderness, and your 139.34 nipped Ghastly by 2.02 in the kind of nail-biter that makes a 1-4 team feel like a playoff contender for exactly one night. Your Elo jumped 18.4 points — the biggest gain of any team this week — and the all-time series against Ghastly is now knotted at four. Last week Ashton Jeanty scored 32.5 and you lost. This week Jeanty had a modest 13.4 and you won. Fantasy football is an absurdist play, and you're the protagonist. Gibbs added 15.7, Herbert posted 15.64, and the "playing for 2026" team just proved it can compete in 2025 on the right day. The war chest is still enormous. The rebuild is still the plan. But the first win is the kind of moment that turns a process into a story, and the group chat finally has something to congratulate you for.

Your kicker scored 19.1 points. Your kicker was your second-highest scorer. Ka'imi Fairbairn at 19.1 trailed only Kendrick Bourne's 19.2, while rookie Jaxson Dart posted 17.58 at quarterback and Justin Jefferson — a top-three dynasty asset — was fourth on your own scoring list with 15.8. That's five weeks of a roster where the supporting cast isn't supporting and the stars aren't starring brightly enough. You scored 146.38, which would have beaten five other teams this week, and lost by 31.56 because you drew the one opponent who decided to go nuclear with 177.94. The preseason called you "a cautionary tale of stars without support." Five weeks in, the tale has become an epic poem nobody wants to read. Your Elo sits at 1323.5, the lowest in the league, and the all-time series against MHJTIME moves to 2-3. The Jefferson trade isn't a rumor anymore — it's a necessity. Do it now and salvage the future. Wait, and the purgatory the preseason warned about becomes permanent residence.

Five games. Zero wins. And the most damning stat isn't the 0-5 record — it's the 605.0 total points for, dead last in the league by nearly 30 points. Jared Goff led with 20.12, Aidan Hutchinson from the DL slot added 15.0, and Ladd McConkey managed 12.4. Davante Adams and Evan Engram tied at 11.3 in a stat line that screams replacement level. The preseason predicted spoiler potential — "knocks contenders out of the playoffs but never raises the trophy." At 0-5, you can't knock on the playoff door, let alone through it. The wagyu beef WRs aren't cooking, and the ramen noodle RBs haven't improved their recipe. Your Elo dropped another 7.3 to 1329.9, and the distance between you and the five teams at 4-1 is widening every week. The chat predicted random 180-point weeks. The season high is still that 147.3 from Week 2. The clock is ticking, and it's your namesake who's keeping time.

confessionals.text: We won. I keep saying it out loud because it doesn't feel real yet. Emeka Egbuka went off for 27.8, some guy named Croskey-Merritt scored 26.0, and we beat Ghastly by two points. Last week Jeanty scored 32.5 and we lost. This week Jeanty scored 13.4 and we won. I've stopped trying to understand fantasy football. The group chat sent exactly one message after the final scores: a single thumbs-up emoji. That's the most respect we've gotten all season.

They said our window was closing. They said the veterans were past their prime. Then Kyren Williams went for 27.1 and we ended the only unbeaten run in the league. Four-and-one. Three straight wins. The preseason ranked us eleventh. I haven't typed a single word in the group chat about it. I'm just quietly updating my playoff scenarios and smiling.

One hundred seventy-seven point ninety-four. I texted that number to the group chat with zero context. No words. Just the number. Ja'Marr Chase remembered he's Ja'Marr Chase. Rico Dowdle — a guy I almost benched — scored 31.9. Two weeks ago this column called my roster a crime scene. I'm framing that paragraph and hanging it in my office. The crime scene just produced the week's highest score by thirty points.

Zero for five against Kittler. In my entire time in this league, I have never beaten that team. JSN scored 23.2. Ferguson scored 20.4. Didn't matter. Jonathan Taylor scored 30.1 and Kittler won by 12 like they always do. I'm starting to think the universe has a restraining order keeping me away from beating bchodos. The side bets are off until further notice.

mailbag.question: Dear Commish: The Lock of the Week has now busted two weeks in a row. Should we rename it the Jinx of the Week?
mailbag.answer: Two straight Locks, two straight losses. At this point the Lock isn't a prediction — it's a warning label for the other team. Legion was favored by 3, lost by 3.58. The column's gambling arm is under federal investigation, but we'll keep swinging because admitting defeat is for teams at 0-5.

mailbag.question: From the group chat: Five teams at 4-1. Has this ever happened before in the Jailyard?
mailbag.answer: Not in league history. The closest was 2023 when three teams started 3-1. Five teams sharing the top record through five weeks is unprecedented, and it means the next three weeks will be a bloodbath separating contenders from pretenders. Place your bets on who falls first — just don't ask the Lock of the Week.

mailbag.question: @rango_ asks: Was 177.94 the best single-week performance in league history?
mailbag.answer: Not close. The Legion of Bouz dropped 248.26 in Week 11 of 2024 — the all-time record. But 177.94 is the highest score of the 2025 season, and coming from a 1-3 team with a "patchwork" RB room, it's arguably the most surprising big number in recent memory. Rico Dowdle's 31.9 leading the charge makes it even more improbable.

mailbag.question: Dear Commish: Chudders won their first game. How much champagne should we allocate?
mailbag.answer: One bottle per win. So far that's one bottle. But Egbuka's 27.8 and Croskey-Merritt's 26.0 suggest the rebuild is producing results earlier than the timeline predicted. Save the case for 2026 — the preview is getting better every week.

mailbag.question: From the group chat: The preseason ranked Noble second. They're ninth. Should we fire the preseason?
mailbag.answer: The preseason assumed Bijan Robinson, Caleb Williams, and A.J. Brown would produce like top-ten assets. Through five weeks, a defense and Javonte Williams are carrying the scoring. We don't fire the preseason — we fire the assumptions. Noble's talent hasn't changed. The execution has.

bits.title: Preseason Prediction Tracker
bits.text: Week 4 picks went 3-3, bringing the cumulative record to 14-10. The Lock of the Week (Legion -3.0 over Sleeping Giants) busted for the second straight week — the Giants won by 3.58. The Upset Watch (Boonist Monks +1.5 over Kittler) also missed. The Stay Away (Chudders vs Ghastly) produced the week's biggest upset. This column's Lock is now 0-2 in the last two weeks. Still positive overall, but the hot streak is decidedly room temperature.

bits.title: Nobody Believes in Us
bits.text: The Sleeping Giants, ranked eleventh in the preseason, are 4-1 and riding a three-game winning streak after ending the league's only unbeaten run. Kyren Williams, Jalen Hurts, and a rotating cast of aging receivers keep producing. Nobody believes them. They keep winning anyway.

bits.title: Luck Index
bits.text: Chudders winning by 2.02 over Ghastly — after losing by 21.36 last week to the Boonist Monks — is the week's luckiest result. The spread between Egbuka's 27.8 and Fields' 25.92 was essentially the margin. Meanwhile, Burden scoring 146.38 and losing by 31.56 is the week's unluckiest outcome. When your best week of the season runs into someone's 177.94, that's not bad roster management — that's cosmic cruelty.

bits.title: Things I Believe But Can't Prove
bits.text: MHJTIME will finish 7-7 after alternating nuclear weeks and disasters for the rest of the season. Kittler will not lose to the Boonist Monks in 2025. Chudders won't win again until Week 9 but will somehow win three straight to close December. And the Lock of the Week will hit next week specifically because nobody expects it to.

bits.title: Ewing Theory Alert
bits.text: Omarion Hampton went from 25.0 last week to 10.0 this week, and Ghastly lost by 2.02. Anti-Ewing Theory in action: when your breakout star regresses, the whole machine stalls. Compare that to MHJTIME, where the breakout star was Rico Dowdle — a guy nobody expected to start — and the machine ran at full speed. Sometimes the Ewing Theory works in reverse: you need the unexpected star more than the expected one.

picks.blurb: The Monks just dropped three spots after Kittler dismantled them by 12.04, and Rasheeing has Josh Allen plus a two-game winning streak. The Monks have the third-most total points in the league at 762.5, so the scoring talent is there, but momentum and Allen's floor favor the Scene in what should be a tight one.

Yes, the Lock has busted two straight weeks. Yes, putting faith in this column's confidence picks requires a certain masochism. But Kittler is the number one seed with the most total points in the league, and MHJTIME's 177.94 feels like a one-week eruption rather than a sustainable floor. Jonathan Taylor's 30.1 against a Jayden Daniels offense that's still finding its legs at 2-3. We ride the defending champion one more time.

Burden is 0-5 and just ran into MHJTIME's nuclear 177.94. Ken-obi is 4-1, bounced back from last week's loss, and has the highest Elo in the league at 1700.2. The franchise everyone measures themselves against shouldn't struggle with the franchise that can't measure a win. Ken-obi rolls.

Both teams are 2-3 and inconsistent. Noble has Bijan Robinson and Breece Hall, two backs who haven't simultaneously produced yet this season. Ghastly is coming off a 2.02-point loss to a 0-4 team and Hampton regressed from 25.0 to 10.0. The preseason two-spot has enough firepower to handle a Ghastly team that can't find consistency. Bijan awakens.

Legion lost its first game but remains 4-1 with Mahomes, McCaffrey, and ARSB. Father Time is 0-5 with the league's lowest point total at 605.0. The bounce-back game writes itself. This is the most predictable outcome of the week, which in Jailyard terms means something absurd will happen.

Chudders just won their first game, riding Egbuka's 27.8 and Croskey-Merritt's 26.0, but one win doesn't change the 1-4 reality. The Sleeping Giants are on a three-game winning streak, just ended the Legion's unbeaten run, and have Kyren Williams running hot. The momentum gap is real, even if Jeanty and Gibbs can make any game interesting.

special_picks.underdog_lock: Noble FFT +1.0 (Bijan Robinson has to explode sometime, and Ghastly is reeling after a loss to an 0-4 team)
special_picks.stay_away: Chudders vs Sleeping Giants (first-win momentum meets a three-game streak — both teams have reasons to feel invincible)
special_picks.teaser: Kittler -1.5 / Ken-obi -5.0 — two 4-1 teams teased down to comfortable margins against opponents with losing records
